relationships.description: A broad product capability groups narrower sub-capabilities, such as 'Payments' containing 'Refund handling', where each sub-capability remains a meaningful ability that could be regrouped under another parent.
relationships.evidence: The product capability map or roadmap document lists the sub-capability nested under the parent capability, with its own identifier that is also referenced elsewhere.

relationships.description: One product capability can only work if another capability is also present, as when 'Order checkout' cannot function without 'Payment processing'.
relationships.evidence: Architecture or roadmap documentation records the prerequisite, or the features realizing the dependent capability call APIs or services that realize the other capability.

relationships.description: The product ability is how the product meets the stated need, so that having the capability satisfies the requirement's shall-statement and its acceptance criteria.
relationships.evidence: A requirements traceability matrix or issue tracker links the requirement ID to the capability, and the acceptance tests for that requirement exercise the features that realize the capability.

relationships.description: The product capability is the product-side ability that makes an ongoing business function, such as Claims Handling or Accounting, concrete and executable.
relationships.evidence: The business capability model or product architecture document maps the product capability to the business function, and the roles that perform that function are the documented users of the capability.

relationships.description: The capability is assigned to a release, version or roadmap phase as part of that milestone's planned scope and is targeted for delivery by its date.
relationships.evidence: The roadmap tool or release plan lists the capability, or its epic, under the milestone or fix-version along with the milestone's target date.

relationships.description: Having the capability moves the product and its stakeholders toward the intended end state described by the goal, without being the goal's sole or measurable fulfillment.
relationships.evidence: Strategy or OKR documentation cites the capability as a contributor to the goal, or the product brief for the capability states the goal as its rationale.

notes: fulfills→requirement partially overlaps with the traceability predicate satisfies/fulfills-requirements; choose one convention. aggregates on capability-to-capability could be confused with composes; aggregation is right only if sub-capabilities can be shared or regrouped.
